subject: Hosted API fit — quickstart endpoints, rate-slice & ops next actions
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@payzen.io>
Cc: security@payzen.io
Date: Thu, 16 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick follow-up + hosted vs dedicated preference + next steps

Thanks again for your time this morning, Samir — great demo and productive questions. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can size the hosted trial and lock the pilot window.

Recap from today's call:
- PayZen use case: invoice classification + short-response summarization for support agents (low-latency assist).
- Primary constraint: start with a hosted evaluation (fast time-to-value) but keep the option to migrate to Dedicated capacity if traffic or data isolation requires it after pilot.
- Security: PayZen's security team wants SOC2 evidence and a short answers doc about KMS/key isolation.

Suggested short-term plan (pilot / 6-week window):
1) Hosted quickstart sandbox (we provide sandbox endpoints + API key).
2) Endpoint mapping: 1 inference endpoint for classification (short context, 512 tokens) + 1 streaming endpoint for agent assist (longer context, up to 2k tokens).
3) Initial rate-slice: start with 150–250 RPS burst-capable, steady-state 40 RPS — we can refine after you share 7-day traffic samples.
4) Prefetch / KV cache: recommend prefix caching for templates to reduce cost — we'll supply config examples.
5) Security checkpoint: we'll send our SOC2 summary and an abbreviated KMS note; your security team can follow up via security@payzen.io.

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-checklist.pdf (pilot checklist) and endpoint-mapping-proposal.csv (suggested mapping).

Next steps for PayZen:
- Share an anonymized traffic sample (RPS, token distribution, typical concurrency) by end of week so we can provision the sandbox slice.
- Confirm any formal procurement timing or required paperwork (PO, NDA).

If hosted is acceptable as the initial mode, we'll provision sandbox access within 48 hours of receiving the traffic sample and confirm rateguard defaults. If you expect immediate data residency or strict VPC-only requirements, flag now and we’ll discuss Dedicated/Private timeline.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a short Ops note that includes endpoint URIs and rate-slice recommendations.

— Mina Haddad
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132
From: Samir Patel <samir@payzen.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: security@payzen.io
Date: Thu, 16 Nov 2028 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + hosted vs dedicated preference + next steps

Thanks, Mina — appreciate the concise plan. Quick clarifications from our side:

1) Deployment preference: we want to run hosted for the pilot (low friction) and evaluate Dedicated for Q2 if the pilot shows steady traffic and we need stronger tenancy isolation.
2) Traffic profile (rough numbers):
   - Avg daily tokens: ~18M tokens/day
   - Avg RPS: 25–45 during business hours
   - Peak concurrency observed during support surges: ~220 concurrent requests (short bursts)
3) Latency target for agent assist: P95 < 300ms (sub-500ms acceptable initially).
4) Security: our InfoSec needs the SOC2 report and a short note on key management (we use AWS KMS). They asked to be CC'd (security@payzen.io).

Timeline: goal is to start pilot next Monday and run 4–6 weeks. Procurement / PO will take ~2 weeks on our side.

I'll upload a small sample traffic CSV to the shared bucket by EOD — ping me if you need a specific schema. Also, we may request a short SLA window for business hours during the pilot.

— Samir
Head of Integrations
PayZen
samir@payzen.io
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@payzen.io>
Cc: security@payzen.io, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Nov 2028 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + hosted vs dedicated preference + next steps

Perfect — thanks for the traffic estimate and timeline. Two concrete items I pushed into this message: an endpoint/rate proposal and what we'll provision for the hosted sandbox.

Endpoint & rate proposal (pilot):
- /v1/infer/classify (sync) — context up to 512 tokens — start: 80 RPS steady, burst to 250 RPS for 90s windows.
- /v1/infer/assist (streaming) — context up to 2k tokens — start: 20 RPS steady, burst to 120 RPS.
- Token budgeting: recommend 1.2x headroom over your avg token/day for pilot prep (we'll size GPUs accordingly).

Operational controls we'll enable for the sandbox:
- Rateguard defaults: conservative throttling to protect latency SLOs; we'll open the burst windows per endpoint as above.
- Canary routing: if you deploy a model update we can route 5% to the new variant by default.
- Prefetch/KV: we'll include a sample prefix caching config in the checklist attachment to reduce repeat compute on template-based calls.

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-checklist.pdf, endpoint-mapping-proposal.csv — both attached. The checklist includes the small JSON snippets you'll drop into your integration for prefix cache and streaming config.

Doc links and pricing: I added links below for the quickstart docs and a DocuSign link to an optional pricing addendum (no commitment required to use sandbox).

If you confirm the pilot numbers, Ben (cc'd) will provision the sandbox slice and I’ll kick off the SOC2 packet send to security@payzen.io.

Next operational step for PayZen: upload the sample CSV and confirm Monday as the pilot start date; I’ll aim to have sandbox credentials to you within 48 hours of the sample.

— Mina
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Nov 2028 16:38:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: PayZen pilot — security packet & sandbox provisioning action items

Ben / Soojin — looping you both in with the rough plan and asks from PayZen. They confirmed hosted for pilot; traffic sketch attached above. Please see suggested owners and timing below.

Tasks:
- Ben: provision a hosted sandbox slice (endpoints + API key) sized for the rates below. Please enable rateguard with burst windows we agreed in the thread and flag if we need a short-term capacity bump for the first 72 hours. Deadline: provision credentials within 48 hours after I confirm the sample CSV.
- Soojin: assemble SOC2 summary + short KMS note (how Redwood handles keys for hosted customers) and send to security@payzen.io. Include a 1-page diagram showing tenant separation. Deadline: 24 hours.
- Mina (me): send endpoint mapping + quickstart snippets to Samir and hand off DocuSign optional addendum if procurement asks for written terms.

Risk notes / escalation path:
- If PayZen's security requests require VPC-only or on-prem during pilot, we should flag Dedicated as a follow-on and have the sales engineering checklist ready (I can start that if needed).
- If observed tail latency >500ms during the pilot, enable canary fallback to a smaller sequence length model to preserve P95.

I'll sync with both of you tomorrow morning if we haven't received the sample CSV by EOD.

— Mina Haddad
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com
